issues.legal_issue: The land was held as a public religious endowment for the temple rather than as the personal property of its manager.
material_facts: The suit sought relief concerning the management of a temple and its endowed property as a public religious trust.

Settlement records stated that the revenue-free status of part of the estate depended on the temple being maintained and described the manager as an ostensible owner, with real ownership vested in the trust.
The deceased manager stated that the property belonged to the deity and that he was only its custodian; the successor affirmed the correctness of that statement in evidence.
The successor also made applications and declarations treating the deity or trust as owner and himself as manager, and representing that the property’s income was used for religious purposes.
issues.conclusion: The estate was a public religious trust or endowment dedicated to the deity, not the personal property of the successor manager.
issues.legal_principle: The settlement records, including a village administration record carrying a presumption of correctness, and the managers’ admissions supported the conclusion that the property vested in the temple or math as a juristic person. An evidentiary admission is not conclusive, but it raises an estoppel and shifts the burden to the person making it or that person’s representative to explain or disprove it; unless explained or shown to be wrong, it is effective proof. The Court distinguished Babu Bhagwan Din v. Gir Har Saroop on its different facts. The dispute arose in a suit under Section 92 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

predicates.public_religious_endowment_dispute: A proceeding concerns whether property associated with a religious institution is a public endowment or the personal property of its manager.
predicates.official_records_connect_property_to_tem: Official settlement or administration records connect the property or its continued revenue-free status to the temple and its maintenance.
predicates.predecessor_admitted_deity_ownership: The former manager stated that the property belonged to the deity and that the manager held it only as custodian.
predicates.successor_confirmed_admission: The successor manager confirmed the former manager’s statement or otherwise treated the deity or trust as owner and himself as manager.

issues.definition: In a dispute over a public religious endowment, official records connecting property to the temple or admissions by the former and successor managers that the deity owns it support treating the property as held for the public religious endowment.

issues.legal_issue: A new statutory-title claim depending on factual matters could not be raised for the first time in the final appeal when it had not been pleaded or argued in the courts below.
material_facts: In the final appeal, the manager advanced an alternative claim that statutory rights had accrued to him personally after the property came into his possession.
That claim had not been set out in his written statement or raised before the courts below.
Deciding the claim required evidence, including evidence about whether the relevant statutory rights had been granted to the manager personally or to the deity or temple.
The manager applied to add the new grounds in the final appeal, and the opposing party objected.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to entertain the new claim because it was raised belatedly and was not a pure question of law.
issues.legal_principle: A new plea that is not raised in the pleadings or considered by the lower courts cannot be entertained at the final appeal stage where its determination depends on evidence and is not a pure question of law. The appellant’s proposed arguments referred to Sections 209, 210, 18 and 6 of the Uttar Pradesh Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950, but the Court did not decide their merits.

rule.if: final_appeal and new_statutory_title_claim and plea_absent_from_lower_court_proceedings and claim_requires_evidence

predicates.final_appeal: A party asks a court of final appeal to determine a claim.
predicates.new_statutory_title_claim: The party advances a claim that personal title or rights arose under a statutory scheme.
predicates.plea_absent_from_lower_court_proceedings: The claim was not included in the party’s pleadings or raised before the lower courts.
predicates.claim_requires_evidence: Determining the claim depends on factual evidence rather than solely on a question of law.

issues.definition: When a party first advances a statutory-title claim in a final appeal, and the claim was absent from the lower-court proceedings and requires evidence, the claim is not entertained.
